RU: синк истории: main принял merge-шишки форка, дерево не тронуто

Замеры 12.11 показали: наш форк `bahooo22/Strata` отставал от локального main на 14 коммитов
(весь набор патчей 11–12.11 — гейт окна #5715, комплект,coder-сетка, вердикт super N=8), а на
форке за это время выросли 5 шишек «Sync fork». Прямого пуша не было: история разошлась.

Что изменено?
- Ни одного файла. Это merge-коммит стратегией `-s ours` против `origin/main` (`8de979c2`):
  дерево результата байт-в-байт равно дереву `37d34a9a`, `git diff --numstat` у коммита пуст по
  построению. Второй родитель нужен только для того, чтобы пуш main стал fast-forward и не
  потребовал force.

Зачем?
- До этой правки пуш main отклонялся как non-fast-forward, и наши патжи жили только на стенде.
  Удаление чужих шишек (force-push) означало бы переписывание запушенной истории, поэтому выбран
  обратимый вариант: принять их как предков, сохранив своё дерево.

Замеры?
- `git merge-base HEAD origin/main` = `13eedf55` = tip `upstream/main`, то есть весь апстрим уже в
  нашей истории (`merge-base --is-ancestor upstream/main HEAD` — да).
- Содержательный долг форка против базы: 83 файла (`git diff --numstat upstream/main origin/main`) —
  наши же прежние версии (LOCAL.*, README, docs/assets/*.svg, packaging/kit/*, CMakeLists), а не чужой код.
- Гейт после мержа: `git diff --exit-code <до> <после>` пуст; `df`-подобных правок нет.

Принятый остаток?
- 5 шишек форка так и остаются пустыми по содержимому — осознанно: их деревья старше наших
  сегодняшних фиксов (fp32-гейт до #5715, прежняя формулировка «N=8 отклонён»), и брать их содержимое
  нельзя.
- Пуш — этим же прогоном после зелёного гейта; CI-аппрувы и тексты PR остаются за пользователем.

Итог
- История форка и локальный main сходятся в один tip, дерево осталось прежним, патчи становятся
  видны на GitHub без force-push.

---

EN: history sync: main accepted the fork's merge bubbles without touching the tree

Measurements on 12.11 showed our fork `bahooo22/Strata` lagged behind local main by 14 commits (the
whole 11–12.11 patch set — the #5715 window gate, the portable kit, the coder grid, the super N=8
verdict), while five "Sync fork" bubbles had accumulated on the fork. A direct push was impossible:
the histories had diverged.

What changed?
- No files at all. This is a merge commit using the `-s ours` strategy against `origin/main`
  (`8de979c2`): the resulting tree is byte-identical to the tree of `37d34a9a`, and the commit's
  `git diff --numstat` is empty by construction. The second parent exists only so that pushing main
  becomes a fast-forward and needs no force.

Why?
- Before this change pushing main was rejected as non-fast-forward, so our patches lived only on the
  stand. Deleting the fork's bubbles (force-push) would rewrite published history, so we took the
  reversible route: adopt them as ancestors and keep our own tree.

Verified?
- `git merge-base HEAD origin/main` = `13eedf55` = tip of `upstream/main`, i.e. the whole upstream is
  already in our history (`merge-base --is-ancestor upstream/main HEAD` — yes).
- The fork's content debt against that base: 83 files (`git diff --numstat upstream/main origin/main`)
  — our own older revisions (LOCAL.*, README, docs/assets/*.svg, packaging/kit/*, CMakeLists), not foreign code.
- Gate after the merge: `git diff --exit-code <before> <after>` is empty.

Accepted remainder?
- The five fork bubbles stay content-empty on purpose: their trees predate today's fixes (the fp32
  gate before #5715, the earlier "N=8 rejected" wording), so their content must not be taken.
- The push runs in this same pass after the green gate; CI approvals and PR texts stay with the user.

Result
- The fork's history and local main now converge on one tip, the tree is unchanged, and the patches
  become visible on GitHub without a force-push.

release_check: the fifth pointer is llama.cpp, and it is content, not a label (W1022)

The engine is built against a vendored llama.cpp tree; nothing in the release record
said which one.  The answer, verified three ways, is 3cf0325 (= tag b11062,
2026-09-20), the same commit the fork pins in .github/workflows/metal-build.yml:29.

  image  /src/third_party/llama.cpp   tree hash 6feee58927d5f1efd38e72bbc1db061d
  baked  ref/llama_3cf0325             same hash
  engine /llama.cpp/ggml/... x93      compiled from that tree

It has not moved since 0.2.8p2: identical 2824 files / 166,037,690 bytes across four
images, so the v0.2.11 rebase changed none of it.

Two things were wrong in the release record and are now checked:
  - BUILD-IMAGE.json carried "3cf0325", a 7-char prefix nothing can be verified against;
  - no tree hash at all, so an image could swap the vendored tree silently.

release_check.py now requires a full 40-hex pin equal to the upstream workflow pin,
and a tree hash recorded at build time and re-computed inside the image.  The
Dockerfile asserts that hash, so a swapped tarball fails the build.

gate: prove the llama.cpp pin check can fail (W1022)

release_check.py grew a fifth pointer and nothing tested it.  ci/selftest_pin.py builds a
throwaway repo per case (workflow pin, _ci_all.txt, a mi50-* tag) so the other four
pointers stay green and a red result can only come from the pin:

  1  correct pin, 93 references          rc=0
  2  upstream pin replaced with f*40     rc=1  pin (release)
  3  no upstream pin declared            rc=1  pin (upstream)
  4  build never touched /llama.cpp      rc=1  in engine build

Wired into round_gate --ci next to the cfg verdict test.  On a runner without docker it
prints SKIP(no docker) and exits 0 -- loudly, because a skip that looks like a pass is
how the last four CI runs stayed red without anyone noticing.

docker: build args, so commits_on_top cannot go stale in the image metadata

The literal 66 in BUILD-IMAGE.json was already wrong by two commits a few minutes
after it was written.  A number nobody re-derives is the exact failure this project
keeps repeating, so the Dockerfile now takes COMMITS_ON_TOP and STRATA_TAG from the
build command (documented in the header) and the tag becomes visible in the image.

release_check: two pin declarations, compared instead of picked

third_party/ggml/VERSION.txt is the declaration CMakeLists.txt:2078 obeys when
STRATA_GGML_DIR is empty; the workflow pin is a second copy of the same fact.  The
first version of this check read only the workflow, i.e. it trusted the copy and
ignored the source.  Now both are read and a disagreement fails:

  VERSION.txt  3cf03257f219afbe7334045ff7c6a06ac68c627d Sun Sep 20 16:08:11 2026 +0800
  workflow     LLAMA_CPP_COMMIT: 3cf03257f219afbe7334045ff7c6a06ac68c627d

Self-test now also covers the disagreement case (4/4).

report_lint: the container table must name ROCm and llama.cpp, checked per row (W1025)

The gate was whole-text: mentioning "llama.cpp" anywhere in the prose satisfied it, which is
exactly how the two dependency versions stayed out of the 10-field table while the report
passed.  Two new fields, both LINE-level and scoped to section 一:

  F9  ROCm        one row with ROCm + a version + HIP/hipconfig/.info/version
  F10 llama.cpp   one row with llama.cpp + bNNNNN + the full 40-hex sha

Why per row: this box carries three different ROCm numbers (packaged 10.1.0, build id
7.14.0-gfx906+…, HIP runtime 7.16.26323), so a whole-text match would accept any of them;
and a 7-char llama.cpp prefix cannot be verified against anything.

report_lint is now 14 checks.  Measured: before adding the rows the same report fails with
"表内 0 行", after adding them PASS (14 fields).  round_gate's positive sample carries the two
rows so its self-test stays honest.

ci: the gate now lives where the push lands, and it caught two real defects on day one (W1028)

GitHub Actions on this fork answer 422 "Actions has been disabled for this repository" to every
dispatch, and /repos/.../actions/permissions reports enabled=true anyway -- so the API cannot be
trusted to say whether CI runs, and nothing has run since #44.  Industry answer: put the gate at
the integration point instead of in the pusher's shell.  /home/albus/strata166/gate/strata-gate.git
is a bare repo whose pre-receive hook unpacks each pushed commit into a temp dir and runs
ci/round_gate.py --ci there.  A green run writes receipts/<sha>.json; ci/deploy.sh step 0 refuses
to deploy a HEAD without one.

Proven both ways, on the receiving end only:
  git push gate gfx906/mi50                        -> GATE PASS, receipt written
  git push --no-verify gate HEAD:tmp/gate-negative -> pre-receive hook declined (BUNDLE.tsv with
                                                      phase_ms 400 instead of 510)

Two defects the first two pushes found, both of the "works where I ran it" family:

1. receive-pack exports GIT_DIR and the quarantine variables, and `git -C <dir>` does NOT
   override them.  The hook's own gate therefore talked to the bare repo instead of the temp
   checkout: `git describe --tags` said "No names found" and a good commit was rejected.  Fixed
   by reading the tree with an explicit --git-dir and running the gate under `env -u GIT_*`.

2. Worse, and pre-existing: ci/selftest_pin.py builds throwaway repos with `git init`, and when
   it ran inside a git hook the exported GIT_DIR made that init re-initialise the REAL worktree.
   It set `core.bare = true` on /home/albus/strata166/pr/strata-fork; every git command then
   failed with "this operation must be run in a work tree" until it was reset.  sh() now strips
   GIT_* and fixture() asserts the temp dir really is a work tree, so this cannot be silent again.

This is the same shape as W1018 (evidence only on my laptop) and W1027 (Actions off, nobody
noticed): the gate has to be somewhere the change cannot avoid.

ci: the red was a hardcoded path, and the gate is GitHub's again (W1029)

Runs #42-#44 failed in 9-11 seconds each.  The log says why, in one line:

  ROUND_GATE: FAIL (1)
    - selftest_pin.py: [BAD] baseline: both declarations agree   rc=2

rc=2 is Python refusing to open a file.  selftest_pin.py had
  RC = "/home/albus/strata166/pr/strata-fork/ci/release_check.py"
-- an absolute path to *my* work repo, which does not exist on a runner.  Every case then
reported a pin failure that had nothing to do with the pin, and the one case that must pass
(baseline) could not.  Now RC is resolved next to __file__, and a missing file raises a clear
SystemExit instead of being scored as "[BAD]".  Proof: a depth-1 clone of this branch -- no work
repo, no tags, exactly what a runner has -- runs `ci/round_gate.py --ci` to PASS, SELFTEST 4/4.

Also in this change:

  * .github/workflows/downstream-gate.yml: checkout with fetch-depth 0 + fetch-tags.  A depth-1
    checkout has no tags and every tag-based check fails for a reason unrelated to the change.
  * ci/gh_gate.py: the deploy gate is GitHub's run now.  `ci/deploy.sh` step 0 asks for a
    completed, successful `downstream-gate` run for the exact HEAD sha; exit 6 = no run / still
    running, 7 = failed (URL printed), 8 = API.  The W1028 local receipt stays, as a note.

One blocker is not in the code: this repository's own Actions switch is off.
  GET  /repos/.../actions/permissions  -> {"enabled": true, "allowed_actions": "all"}
  PUT  same endpoint                   -> 204
  POST .../downstream-gate.yml/dispatches -> 422 "Actions has been disabled for this repository"
  same call on phoenixclyde/vllm-gfx906-routeb (not a fork) -> 422 "does not have workflow_dispatch
  trigger", i.e. Actions answers normally there, so it is this repo, not the account.
No API flips that switch; the Actions tab's banner (or Settings -> Actions -> General) does.
Until then gh_gate.py exits 6 and deploys are refused -- which is the point: a gate that can be
skipped when the cloud is inconvenient is not a gate.

ci: empty commit to trigger the first run after Actions was re-enabled

GitHub does not backfill runs for commits pushed while Actions was off, so enabling the switch
has to be followed by a push.  Nothing in the tree changes.

docs: the four steps that actually turn Actions on for a fork (W1029)

workflow_dispatch answering 422 while actions/permissions says enabled:true is not a
contradiction: one is the fork-level enablement, the other is the policy.  Settings ->
Actions -> General is necessary but not sufficient -- the Actions tab banner is the second
switch -- and GitHub never backfills a run for a sha pushed while Actions was off (empty
commit e4f0867d: 180 s, no run).  deploy/ is not tracked here, so this lives in ci/README.md
and the workflow comment now points there instead of at a file only my laptop has.

ci: the second red was a host fact scored as a release failure (W1029)

Run #45 (the first one after Actions was re-enabled) failed at the round gate with:

  - selftest_pin.py: [BAD] baseline: both declarations agree  rc=1
      [FAIL] container image  error: no such object: strata166-407

That is `docker inspect` on a runner that has docker but not our container.  The pin self-test
was judging five rows that only exist on the build box (container image, BUILD-IMAGE.json,
binary, engine versions agree, llama.cpp tree).  A host fact is not a release fact: on a runner
the honest answer is SKIP, not FAIL.

release_check.py grew `--offline`, which turns exactly those five rows into SKIP (the tag, pin and
engine-build rows are still judged -- they are what a static run can actually check), and
selftest_pin.py now calls it with `--offline`.

Verified where it matters: `ci/selftest_pin.py` is 4/4, `release_check.py --offline` is PASS with
five SKIPs named as such.  The next GitHub run is the judge.

Two leaks in two runs, both the same shape: a check that quietly assumed the machine it was
written on.  First the absolute path to release_check.py, now the container name.

ci: judge the recipe when there is no image, and give the fixture one (W1029)

Run #46 got one row further and stopped at:

  [BAD] baseline ... rc=1 | [FAIL] llama.cpp pin (release) (absent)

Correct diagnosis: --offline skipped BUILD-IMAGE.json, and the release pin row then read that
same absent file.  Two fixes, both about judging the right object:

  * offline, the release pin is read from ci/docker/Dockerfile-* (the recipe that bakes the pin
    in), so the row still means something on a runner instead of being skipped or absent;
  * the self-test fixture now writes that Dockerfile too, because a fixture that lacks a file
    the check reads is not a repo -- it was "absent" for every case, including baseline.

Verified in a clean depth-1 clone with no container and no /data (what a runner is):
ROUND_GATE PASS, SELFTEST 4/4.

Three reds, three environment assumptions: an absolute path, a container name, and a fixture
that was not the shape of the thing it stood for.

gfx906: compile the HIP virtual-memory path (the elastic K/V, --kv-grow)

The HIP implementation was excluded on gfx906 by `!defined(STRATA_HIP_GFX906)`, with the comment
"gfx906: no virtual memory". Measured on this MI50 with this ROCm (10.1.0, self-built gfx906 tree):

  hipDeviceAttributeVirtualMemoryManagementSupported = 1
  hipMemGetAllocationGranularity = 4096 B
  hipMemAddressReserve(64 MiB) / hipMemCreate / hipMemMap / hipMemSetAccess -> all hipSuccess
  two chunks mapped at different offsets: write/read both correct
  after unmap + release of one chunk the other still reads back correctly  <- what --kv-grow needs

So the exclusion was an assumption about the hardware, not a fact.  It is also redundant: the
implementation already fails closed on the runtime attribute, and nothing turns the elastic K/V on
by itself (--kv-grow / STRATA_KV_GROW plus generate.cpp's eleven conditions).

Also note the guard has to be an OR: this tree's gfx906 TUs get -DSTRATA_HIP_GFX906=1 but NOT
-DSTRATA_USE_HIP (build.ninja, every target but dflash2.cpp), so `#if defined(STRATA_USE_HIP)` alone
compiles the stub again and the binary does not change at all (md5 stayed d24f8293 on the first try).

gfx906: rows-per-wavefront table for the Q8_0 wave kernel (single-request decode GEMV)

A single-request decode runs a speculative verify window, so native_mmvq is called with
ncols > 1.  Per weight block the kernel then issues NCOLS times the activation loads and
dp4a work, and wave_launch_n hardcoded R = 1: one row per wavefront, none of that work
shared.  Measured on the shapes that matter at ncols 6, R = 2 gives 1.6-1.8x and R = 4
gives 1.9x on qkv/gate/q, and the whole layer goes 613.6 -> 385.4 us.

The table is measured, not a formula: 9 shapes x ncols 1..8 x R in {1,2,4} on the real

perf(gr): record why a 34-byte Q8_0 block cannot take a 32-bit load; add the roofline probe

R28 asked whether the HC down kernel could replace its 32 scalar 2-byte loads with wide
loads. It cannot: a Q8_0 block is 2 + 32 = 34 bytes, so a block starts at 0 or 2 mod 4 and a
32-bit load of `q` is misaligned half the time (undefined on GCN). Widening would require
padding the pack format to 36 bytes, which is a format change, not a kernel change. The
arithmetic now lives next to the loads so nobody re-derives it wrongly.

ci/probe/stream_roof.cpp measures what every "% of peak" claim in the plan had been guessing
at: the achievable read roof on this card. Measured 884 GB/s (86.3% of the 1024 GB/s spec),
copy roof 752 GB/s, and a parallelism curve that peaks at 4 blocks/CU (1 block/CU only
reaches 55%). Decode reads and writes almost nothing, so 884 -- not 1024, and certainly not
the ~700 that was in use -- is the denominator.

Consequence: dense decode sits at 29.8% of the roof (was reported as 37%), and even the best
single kernel (native_mmvq at 2560x10240, ncols=2) only reaches 53%.

perf(decode): measure what actually limits the hyper-connection read

The plan had three candidate explanations for HC reading 644 MiB in 6.89 ms and none of them
had been separated: bandwidth, parallelism (block count), or load width (a 34-byte Q8_0 block
cannot take a 32-bit load, so the kernel issues 17 two-byte loads per block).

ci/probe/read_probe.cpp isolates them. Same bytes, one variable at a time:

  mode0  17 x 2-byte loads per block    (what the kernel does today)
  mode1  16-byte streaming loads        (the ceiling if LDS staging worked)
  S      split the reduction S ways     (bytes constant, only the block count moves)

gfx906, alongside production:
  HC down 10240->320   S=1  553 / 613 GB/s      S=4  621 / 826      S=8  494 / 493
  GDN      2560->10240 S=1  566 / 763
  HC up     320->10240 S=1  125 (row is 340 B, not a multiple of 16 -> no wide read at all)

So split-K buys +12% with a knee at S=4, wide loads buy +11..35%, and the two compose to
+49%. But the number that matters is the comparison nobody had made: production HC runs at
98 GB/s while the crudest 2-byte read of the same bytes runs at 553. Load pattern is worth at
most 1.5x of the gap; the other 5.6x is inside the fused kernel (norm, cross-lane reduction,
LDS round trip, up projection) or in occupancy.

That inverts the previous plan: the wide-load rewrite is demoted, and the next experiment is to
rebuild the probe one step at a time until it becomes the real kernel, measuring the bandwidth
lost at each step.

Two measurement traps are documented in the file, because both were hit: re-reading the same
rows each pass turned the measurement into an L2 test (1.5 TB/s, above the HBM roof), and an
`if (result == impossible) store` keep-alive was optimised away together with the loads.

perf(decode): the hyper-connection read is not bandwidth bound, it is arithmetic bound

The previous probe showed a pure read of the HC tensors running at 581-666 GB/s while production
manages 98, so the load pattern could explain at most 1.5x of the gap. Adding the arithmetic
closes the accounting.

Two more modes, same bytes, one variable at a time:
  gemv  the same 17 x 2-byte loads, then Q8 dequantise and FMA against an LDS activation tile
  pad   identical to gemv except the per-lane activation stride is 33 floats instead of 32

  HC down 10240->320  S=1   read 581   wide 636   gemv 255   pad 348 GB/s
  GDN     2560->10240 S=1   read 631   wide 708   gemv  98   pad 173
  big     10240->8192 S=1   read 666   wide 800   gemv 264   pad 353

So: dequantise + FMA costs 2.5-6x, and it reproduces production (98) exactly. Widening the load
only helps when there is no arithmetic (708 -> 98 at S=1). The kernel moves 32 bytes per Q8_0
block and spends 32 converts plus 32 FMAs on them -- about 2 ALU ops per byte -- and that, not
HBM, is the wall.

The second finding is a bank conflict. A per-lane stride of 32 floats puts every lane in the same
LDS bank; padding to 33 recovers 36-76%. The production kernel indexes xs[k][v] with
v = 32*(4s+bl) + 4*sub, so v mod 32 = (4*sub) mod 32 is independent of the lane -- the same
pathology. Changing that is a candidate that keeps the summation order, so it can be held to
diff = 0.

Occupancy, taken from the shipped device assembly rather than guessed: the down kernel uses 119
VGPRs at T=2 (25% occupancy) and 140 at T=3, which crosses the 128 line and halves occupancy to
12.5%. The _fast_ variant exists to stay at 128 and only helps at T=3; at T=2 it changes nothing
for down and costs up 12.5 points (62.5 -> 50), so STRATA_TSUM=1 is not a win here.

perf(decode): dp4a is worth 73-117% on the arithmetic-bound read, and a retracted bank-conflict claim

Two things, one probe.

First, the measured one. The previous round showed dequant + FMA costing 2.5-6x against a pure
read of the same bytes, so the per-byte arithmetic is the wall. gfx906 has v_dot4_i32_i8, so the
probe gained a mode that keeps the loads identical and swaps 32 converts + 32 FMAs for 8 dp4a:

  HC down 10240->320  S=1   read 658   dequant+FMA 262   dp4a 454 GB/s   (+73%)
  GDN     2560->10240 S=1   read 630   dequant+FMA  97   dp4a 211         (+117%)
  big     10240->8192 S=1   read 665   dequant+FMA 263   dp4a 472         (+79%)

At S=1 dp4a reaches 69% of the pure-read number. That is the whole case for it: 2 ALU ops per
byte down to about 0.5. The cost is that activations must be int8 as well, which changes the
numerics and therefore has to pass the decode gate; and the only dp4a path already in the tree
covers "up" alone, compiled out for gfx906 by `#if !STRATA_GR_FAST_BUILD`.

Second, the retraction. The previous commit claimed the production xs[k][v] read suffers a 32-way
LDS bank conflict. It does not. I had read `v = 32*(4*s + bl) + 4*sub` but not the line above it:
`sub = lane & 7, bl = lane >> 3`. With those, a b128 read splits into phases of eight lanes whose
start banks are 0/4/8/.../28 -- all 32 banks, no conflict. The 36-76% that padding "recovered" was
recovering a pathology I had invented in the probe itself (`xs[32*lane + i]`, a 128-byte lane
stride, exactly 32 banks).

Lesson recorded in the plan as rule 2c: before carrying a kernel's conclusion to another kernel,
write out the index arithmetic and count the banks.

docs(decode): the window budget, and a correction about dp4a

Two things the plan had wrong, both caught by looking at more than one phase table.

First, the budget. Every HC number in the plan came from a single table (6.89 ms). Taking the
median of all 123 tables the engine has logged, at 47.22 ms per window:

  expert read   11.78 ms  24.9%   (VRAM hits 8.85 + waitB 1.28 + PCIe 0.81 + copy 0.84)
  HC             7.49 ms  15.9%   (down 3.46 / up 3.44 / norm 0.59)
  router+plan    3.80 ms   8.0%
  q8+qkv gemv    3.24 ms   6.9%

So the largest block in a decode window is the expert read, not the hyper-connection read, and
its byte count has never been worked out. At 400 GB/s, 11.78 ms implies ~4.7 GB per window --
more than the dense weights (4.26 GB). That points at "reading too much" rather than "reading
too slowly", which is a routing/residency question, not a kernel one.

Second, the correction. The previous commit said the dp4a path "exists but is compiled out for
gfx906". It does not exist. There is no __dp4a or sdot4 anywhere in the HC kernels; the four
other hits in the tree are comments, and the one real user is the DeepSeek path. The kernel
whose name suggested otherwise (gr_up_q8_q32_kernel) is a quantise-the-output variant.

And that matters because upstream measured what int8 activations cost: 0.9498% relative
difference against FP16, which is why they deferred dp4a themselves. Add that to writing two new
kernels for 15.9% of the window and the priority order changes: build the expert-read ledger
first, then look at routing, then consider dp4a.

probe: R x S interaction and launch granularity -- two conclusions reversed

R and S were only ever swept one at a time. Both change parallelism, but R merges the output
axis while S cuts the reduction axis, so their effects on locality run in opposite directions
and a single-variable sweep cannot see the interaction. rs_probe sweeps both and deliberately
gives several (R,S) pairs the same block count, which is what makes the comparison meaningful.

What came out:

  * expert shape -- rows with equal block count agree within 2% (32 blocks: R1S4 553, R2S8 554,
    R4S16 564 GB/s). R and S are interchangeable there. Optimum is 32-64 blocks (0.5-1.1/CU).
  * HC down -- with arithmetic the optimum moves left: fma is flat at 520-548 for S=1..4 and
    falls to 358-403 at S=16. Production runs S=16 (Q8_KC 640, Q8_NKC 16), i.e. the right edge.
  * no strong interaction in the arithmetic modes, which rules out grid shape as the cause of
    the HC gap -- a negative result that is worth as much as a positive one.

launch_probe holds total bytes fixed and varies only how many launches it takes to read them:
rep=1 (production's shape, one small kernel per layer) 260 GB/s, rep=128 (fully batched) 458.
Batching is worth 1.76x, but production's 97 GB/s is still 2.7x below the rep=1 probe, so the
launch cost is not the whole story.

This also corrects two earlier numbers of ours:

  * R32's "5.6x is the arithmetic" is withdrawn. That collapse came from the probe filling a
    8 KB LDS tile once per block -- up to 5.7x the data volume. With the tile in registers the
    same conditions hold 528-548 GB/s, so arithmetic costs about 18%, not 5.6x.
  * R35's dp4a "+73..117%" is withdrawn. That compared fma over a 32-way-conflicted LDS tile

probe: TTFT and prefix reuse -- incremental prompts get no reuse at all

Every measurement here has been decode. A single-stream user feels prefill first, and
--prompt-cache-every / --conversation-cache-mib exist to cut that on later turns.

Measured against the live service, streaming, timing the first chunk that carries a token
(the role delta arrives immediately and would report the round trip: 2.4 ms for 1912 tokens):

  cold prefill   349 tok 843 ms (414 tok/s) ... 9707 tok 6915 ms (1404 tok/s)
                 throughput rises with length, i.e. ~800 ms of fixed cost
                 TTFT CV is 71-96%, an order of magnitude worse than decode's 3.9-4.4%,
                 so any prefill A/B needs n>=6 and must report its CV

  same prompt again      3685 -> 252 ms (14.6x): exact-match reuse works
  turn 2 = turn 1 + 400  4418 ms, while a fresh 2903-token prompt takes 4411 ms
                         => an incremental prompt pays 100.2% of the full cost

Root cause, from the source: neither checkpoint mechanism can fire for a 2-4K conversation.
periodic_checkpoint needs done >= --prompt-cache-every (8192 here). tail_checkpoint needs
--prompt-cache-tail (not set) and total-done <= chunk, and with --prefill auto the chunk is
8192 so a 2-4K prompt is a single chunk with nothing left over. --prompt-cache 6 only covers
an identical prompt, not a continuation.

Fix is a parameter: --prompt-cache-every 1024.

probe: is an incremental prompt ever served from cache? no -- and the parameter does not change it

prefill_ab measures TTFT(turn 2 = turn 1 + N new tokens) / TTFT(an equally long prompt that
shares nothing). 100% means every turn pays full prefill. n runs, fresh conversation each,
median plus CV, because prefill's noise is an order of magnitude worse than decode's.

Baseline and the same measurement after --prompt-cache-every 8192 -> 1024 came out identical:
99% then 100%, CV 1% both times. The parameter is inert for this; the log says why.

  prompt 3066 tokens = 0 reused    + 3066 read in 4747 ms
  prompt 3066 tokens = 3061 reused + 5    read in  225 ms   (same prompt again)
  prompt 2903 tokens = 0 reused    + 2903 read in 4546 ms   (previous turn + 400 tokens)
  conversation cache: parked=4 bytes=1083214768 reused_kv_bytes=0

So the cache holds 1.08 GB across four parked conversations and gives none of it back unless a
request matches a previous prompt exactly. Reverting the parameter: at 1024 a 10K prompt takes
nine checkpoints, each a K/V copy, and none of them can be hit by a growing conversation.

The fix belongs upstream: let a checkpoint serve a prompt that extends it. Same K/V, same token
positions, so the output is identical. Recorded as candidate C4 in deploy/UPSTREAM_CONTRIB.md.

probe: real multi-turn shape -- the engine already reuses 80% of the prefix

The previous probe built turn 2 as "turn 1 plus new words", skipping the model's own reply. A
real second turn is [user P1][assistant reply1][user P2], and a parked conversation holds exactly
P1+reply1. Without the reply the prompts diverge at the first new token, so the earlier "0 reused"
was the right answer to the wrong question -- and I nearly reported it upstream as a missing
feature. It is not missing: conversation_prefix() is a prefix test, ConversationCache::best()
takes the longest prefix, borrows()/take() decide borrow versus take.

Measured on the live service, n=3, turn 2 against a single prompt of the same total length:

  turn2   2214 / 2207 / 2044 ms      single   4351 / 4306 / 4231 ms      ratio 51 / 51 / 48 %

log, verbatim:

  prompt 2336 tokens = 1867 reused + 469 read in 1586 ms (295.7 tok/s), 2 checkpoints
  prompt 2333 tokens =    0 reused + 2333 read in 3750 ms (622.1 tok/s), 1 checkpoints

80% reused, TTFT 2.4x. What is left is not the match, it is the restore: 469 tokens are worth
about 754 ms at the control's rate, but the turn took 1586 ms, so roughly 830 ms goes to
restoring the parked K/V and mounting its checkpoint -- 260 MB of snapshot in 0.8 s, about
300 MB/s, far below what PCIe can do. That is the next target, not the matching.

Withdraws candidate C4 in deploy/UPSTREAM_CONTRIB.md and entry R41 in the progress ledger.

glm4: enforce Solar's own generation format at the sampling step

Upstage's vLLM ships `SolarOpenTemplateLogitsProcessor` for exactly this: the model knows its template's format but
is free to leave it, so their serving masks every step.  Without that we measured Qwen's `<tool_call>name
key="value"</tool_call>`, a call with `<|tool_call:name|>` left out, and `<tool_call>[execute]</tool_call>` with the
payload in a fence - all of which ended the agent's turn with nothing done.

The engine samples on the host (host_logits -> sample), so the mask is a state machine plus a few comparisons
(include/strata/glm4/tmpl_mask.hpp, no CUDA):

  start            <|content|>, and <|tool_calls|> when the request has tools
  content          regular tokens and <|flush|>; <|end|> is folded into <|flush|> as the template does
  tool_calls       <|tool_call:begin|> only
  call id          regular tokens, <|tool_call:name|> after ten
  call name        regular tokens and <|tool_call:args|>
  call args        regular tokens and <|tool_call:end|>
  after a call     <|tool_call:begin|> or <|calls|>

The server sends `strata_glm4_tmpl=1|2` when its template wrote the empty think block (effort minimal/low) and the
pack's marker ids are the ones the mask hardcodes; thinking and other families keep the free sampler.

EN: recommend.py: window gate accounts for KV quantum (#5715)

Fix #5715: previously `recommend.py` substituted only `q4_0` into the KV price, there was no
quantum flag, and an answer with a foreign quantum looked like a "measured window". Now the
quantum is a parameter (`--kv-type`), the quantum sets are taken from the engines (Strata: fp32,
q8_0, q5_1, q5_0, q4_0; llama: nine types), an engine with an unsuitable quantum is set aside
with a warning, absence of candidates is a refusal with a reason, and the "measuredness" of the
window is downgraded to a calculation if the quantum differs from the one taken in the ladder.

What changed?
- packaging/kit/recommend.py (+128/-32): added `KV_BY_ENGINE` dictionary with quantum sets for
  each engine (lines 51-60), `KV_MEASURED` constant to mark the measured quantum (61), functions
  `fit_strata`, `fit_llama`, `build_args` gained `kv_type` parameter with default `q4_0` (236, 248,
  263, 277), `kv_bytes_per_token` calls pass the specific quantum from the dictionary (237, 249),
  the launch line substitutes `--kv-type` from the parameter, not from a fixed field (277);
- docs/reports/2026-11-11-portable-kit.md (+47/-18): updated cold3 numbers (304,711,168 /
  225,454,592 instead of 304,716,288 / 225,460,736), added items 6-7 to "Fixed during acceptance"
  (about the merged elf measure and the KV quantum gate), updated "Package built locally" section
  (cold3 + repack after #327), added caveat about KV quantum in "Limits and what remains";
- docs/reports/2026-11-11-portable-kit.ru.md: mirror updated text in Russian.

Why?
The window gate must honestly sign for which KV quantum it is counting the price. Without this, a
user with a q5_1 model would get the answer "measured window 229376", although the ladder was taken
on q4_0, and the KV price for q5_1 is different. Now an answer with a foreign quantum is signed
`basis=formula`, `measured=false` with a warning, and the user sees that the window is calculated,
not measured.

Verified?
- selftest recommend.py: 63/63 controls, rc=0 (was 11/11 before the fix: added KV quantum block,
  two sabotage controls, determinism of two calls);
- leakcheck --prose over 7 kit files: "Чисто.", rc=0;
- portability: grep `D:\`, `F:\`, `C:\Users` over the kit tree — 0 matches;
- SHA gate 4k: e3948d639675 PASS (after cold3 repack);
- live smoke 96k: pp 1176.8 / tg 16.0, 128k: pp 912.1 / tg 15.1 (both basis=formula, launch

Accepted remainder?
- The KV quantum is not signed in `models.json`: the entire ladder was taken on `q4_0`. The KV
  quantum grid is a separate GPU task.
- Issue #5715 and PR texts — for the user.

The window gate knows for which KV quantum it is counting the price and honestly signs the
"measuredness" of the answer. Default behavior has not changed (the output of the old and new
versions is byte-equal after removing the new `kv_type` fields), but an answer with a foreign
quantum is now a calculation, not a measurement.

The mirror of commit 0f37b86e from kit-all into the main tree. The pre-allocation gate that came
from upstream priced the conversation memory at fp32 for every quant type: at q4_0 it asked for
roughly seven times too much and refused contexts the allocation passed with room to spare.

What changed?
- src/qwen35/q36_engine.cu (+7/-2): the fp32 figure moved into `kv_tok_f32` (:1793), while `kv_tok`
  (:1797-1798) is now taken at the quant's own rate, exactly as `alloc_session` asks for it:
  `g.n_head_kv * g.head_dim * 2 / 32 * kv_block_bytes(kv_type) * n_attn`. The comment
  (:1794-1796) explains why the fp32 estimate is only valid at `KV_F32`. The `state` field in the
  `one_session_fit` call (:1808) stays `per - kv_tok_f32 * ctx`: `per` is computed in fp32, and
  subtracting the quantized figure would overflow `size_t`.
- include/strata/qwen35/context_fit.hpp (+1/-1): the comment on the `kv_tok` field (:24) now
  matches - the session's K / V per token at its own quant.

fit on someone else's machine, and `recommend.py`'s warning about an over-long context lied.

q36: host tests for the window draws: top-M kernels, the plain path's draws, the target distribution

Host only (g++, no GPU, no model), run by tools/test_q36_spec_sampling.py: the float keys the kernels order logits by; the kernels'
two-stage top-M run on the host as they are written, against a sort by (logit, lowest id); a window row against the plain sampler on the whole
row (penalized tokens at the top, ties at the cap, a cap of 64 with a window of 64): the same token and the same draw; a whole answer
through windows against the one-token-a-step loop for the same seed (end token and max_new inside a window, right, wrong and
out-of-vocabulary drafts); the accept / reject rule against a known target on a Markov model (a fixed seed; a rule that takes any
candidate draft, and one that takes the draft's own row, are caught); the point-mass case of the Flash-Next rule (core/spec_prob.hpp); the
plain sampler against the code it replaced; and which requests draft.

q36: a sampled request drafts, with the plain path's draws

A request with a temperature above 0 (every request that leaves the temperature out gets the card's 0.7 or 1.0) ran one token a step, 27
tok/s against 65-81 for a greedy one.  It uses the verify window of the previous commit: the host draws row 0 as the plain sampler would
(penalties, the cap, temperature, min_p, top_p, one draw of the request's stream), keeps draft 0 if the draw equals it, then draws row 1,
and so on; the first miss ends the window and its draw is the next token.  Every emitted token is one draw of the row's own target
distribution given the tokens before it, so the output distribution is the plain path's; the draft only decides how many rows are looked
at.  The draft is the draft head's argmax, a point mass, so the Leviathan rule min(1, p / q) accepts with probability p(d), which is the
chance this rule has, and a rejected row's token is a draw from p given that it differs from d.

The random stream is used once per emitted token, in order, as the plain path does, so the same seed gives the same text with and
without drafts when the window rows' logits equal the single-step logits bit for bit (the port's identity check; not measured on
this tree).  A seeded request is reproducible in any case.

The serve loop kept the plain path's draw at the top of every step; after a window the token is already drawn, so a flag skips it.
STRATA_Q36_SPEC_SAMPLE=0 restores the plain path for sampled requests.

q36: a greedy request with a penalty drafts, and its text is the plain path's

The draft is used only when the device argmax can serve the request, so a request with a presence, frequency or repeat penalty
(the instruct set of the model card has presence 1.5) ran one token a step.  A verify window of such a request now returns, for each
row, the M highest raw logits (a two-stage top-M kernel pair in the second graph variant, key 70000, one copy for the window); the host
applies the penalties to the listed tokens that are in the row's window (the last last_n tokens, then the accepted drafts before the
row), ranks them as the sampler does, takes the argmax and compares it with the draft.  Row t is looked at only after rows before it
matched, the first miss ends the window, and the commit of the accepted rows is the greedy path's.

The penalties go on the host, with the plain sampler's own function for one logit, so the two paths run one compiled expression.  That
is exact when M >= the cap + the penalized tokens of the row and every penalty only lowers a logit; a request outside that (a
penalty that raises a logit, a window over 64 or of the whole history) keeps the plain path.  The plain sampler ranks candidates by
(logit, lowest id) now, so an exact tie no longer depends on partial_sort; that is the only change to the plain path.

STRATA_Q36_SPEC_PEN=0 restores the plain path for these requests.  STRATA_Q36_SPEC_CHECK=1 compares each window's rows with the host's
top M of the whole row.  The greedy graph and its code path are unchanged.

[GUI] a damaged chat file has a surface, and its delete clears the row (#5421)

Problem: a chat file the host cannot parse (a hand-edited file, a truncated
one, a `{v:2}` file from a later release) was named in `chatStore.list()`'s
`damaged` array, shipped over `/api/chats`, typed in `chat-sync.ts` - and

until the host restarted, because `remove()` cleared the index but not the
`damaged` set (`save()` cleared both).

Result: one line in `remove()`, mirroring `save()` - `damaged.delete(id)`
beside `index.delete(id)` - and the list has a surface. `hydrateChats` hands
the page the damaged ids, the store keeps them in `damagedChats`, and the
sidebar lists each file under the workspaces as "Unreadable chats" with a
delete and a confirm. A delete in another window clears the row here too:
the `chats` event's `deleted` branch drops the id from that list, and the
after-the-host-was-away sync replaces the whole list from the host.

Sampled requests keep their drafts by the number each position is drawn with

A sampled request draws position i's token with u = Philox(seed, i) through its chain's sorted list, and a draft
passes only as the token drawn. The number is a function of the seed and the position, so it is known when the draft
is made. The draft stays the draft layer's likeliest token: on dumped rounds the token the number selects in the
draft's own distribution is the text's token no more often (first drafts 76.2% against 76.0%). What the number tells
is whether the likeliest token passes: it does when it is the verifier's likeliest too and u falls inside its
interval there, [0, P0). core/draft_pass.hpp gives that chance per chain step from the draft's probability q, u and
the temperature T,

    sigmoid(c + d logit(q)) * sigmoid((a0 + a1 / T + (b0 + b1 / T) logit(q) - logit(u)) / exp(w0 + w1 log T))

fitted on 405 dumped sampled requests of mtp/rt-distilled under IQ3_S and UD-Q4_K_XL (301K tokens; one set of
constants: each file's log loss within 0.0003 of a fit of its own at temperatures 0.3-1.5, the first draft 0.30-0.31
where the layer's own probability scores 0.37). The first draft at q 0.7-0.8 passes 72% of the time under u < 0.5
and 17% from 0.9 on.

--spec-min-p stays a probability under the draft layer: a draft is kept when its chance under its own number is at
least the chance a draft at the floor has under an average number (draft_pass_floor: the formula's mean over u; 0.5
at temperature 0.7 is 0.36 / 0.35 / 0.35 at steps 1-3, where the chance's floor measured best). A number that leaves
the likeliest token room keeps a draft the plain floor would drop, one that has already lost it drops a draft the
plain floor would keep, and toward a temperature of 0 the rule is the plain floor. Greedy requests, requests with
penalties and LAMINA_DRAFT_PASS=0 keep the plain floor.

- MtpDrafter::set_sampling; draft() decides which drafts are kept (n_kept: the next window's drafts, where the
  loops read the probabilities themselves), on_draft(j, token, kept), chances()
- kernels/sampler.hpp: philox_uniform, one definition for the kernels and the host
- generate mode: --temperature, --top-p, --top-k, --min-p, --seed (a sampled run; with --spec-follow along a sampled
  reference of that seed, sampled fixed text)
- --dump-draft-data: a round's record with the drafts' chances and the kept count
- draft_pass_test (CPU): the host's number, the chance, the floor, the fit's values; sampler_parity checks the
  header's Philox against its own writing of it

Measured on the three GPUs, the rule against LAMINA_DRAFT_PASS=0 from one binary, on sampled fixed text (each run
follows a reference drawn at temperature 0.7, top_p 0.95, top_k 20 with its seed; 4 rounds in both orders; IQ3_S /

EN: kit: an empty selection dump stops failing silently
The 4.5 "one click" gate went red against a live model with "the selection has no launch line",
and that line lies: the selection does produce a launch line, while `run/recommend.json` came out
empty because the Python process printed nothing. The reason was drowned in `$null`, so the
measure could not tell "the kit could not pick a window" from "the wrapper could not write it".

discards stderr — `2> $recErr` puts it into `run/recommend.err.log`, the Python exit code is
captured into `$jsrc` before `ErrorActionPreference` changes, and a length check in front of the
JSON parse turns an empty `recommend.json` into "recommend.py --json printed nothing (rc=…)"
carrying the last three stderr lines in the message itself. `2>$null` was the trap: `Out-File`
creates and truncates the file before the first line of output, so a silent child read as
"the launch key is missing". `packaging/kit/start.ps1` (+12/-1) and
`bench-3060ti/kit/start.ps1` (+12/-1) are the same source-of-truth copies in both forks, because
gate 4.6 compares them by md5 with CRLF stripped.

rc=2 refusals with a stated cause"); a reasonless refusal is a silent success run backwards, and
it already cost one red sweep.

cause on stderr and returns 3 — the run yields rc=2 and the new message, so the branch is not
dead code. Positive path: `start.ps1 -DryRun` against a live model writes a 5301-byte

the selection" with zero red lines. All three copies hash to `044f5595fce5` after CRLF stripping.

stand paths in both the tree and the sources.

never enters the archive, but it does stay in the stand tree after runs.

to guess which process died.

--second-gpu-clocks: a refused lock names its clock and its reason; choosing the values for another card

A refused lock was reported with NVML's error and "(the lock needs administrator rights)", whatever the error. NVML
has the graphics clock's lock from Volta on (the RTX 20 series) and the memory clock's from Ampere on (the RTX 30
series): a card without one answers "Not Supported", and the hint sent its user after rights. The line now names the
clock that was refused and adds the rights (root on Linux) to NVML's "Insufficient Permissions" alone.

The switch checked for PCs other than the development one:
- An engine without administrator rights (a token whose Administrators group is deny-only): one line, "GPU 2's
  graphics clock could not be locked (Insufficient Permissions: the lock needs administrator rights, root on Linux):
  it runs at the driver's clocks", then IQ3_S's thinking text at the driver's-clocks speed (143.6 t/s; 171.9 locked)
  and the card idle after. This path had not run before.
- NVML takes values outside a card's range without a word (nvidia-smi's locks on the idle RTX 3090, whose highest
  clocks are 2,100 / 9,751 MHz): an RTX 5060 Ti's 2700-3090/14001 held it at 1,965 / 9,751 MHz and 149 W against
  114 W at 1395-2100/9751, 50-100/100 locked nothing, a memory clock of 7,000 gave 9,501. The usage text and
  examples/README.md tell how to read a card's highest clocks (nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,clocks.max.graphics,
  clocks.max.memory --format=csv).
- Which tier needs it: the same RTX 3090 as the only tier (two GPUs), fixed text, IQ3_S and UD-Q4_K_XL, 2 rounds in
  both orders: at the driver's clocks its rounds are 0.86 +- 0.40% longer than under the lock (11 of 16 pairs;
  thinking text 1.3-3.4%, the others -1.4 to +3.9%), where as the third GPU they are 4-22% longer. With more to do
  the card keeps its clocks (its memory clock 5.2-9.5 GHz on average without a lock).
- The sources compile for Linux (zig's clang; gpu_select.cpp with -Wall -Wextra clean). No Linux driver was measured.

GPU tiers: the startup probe times on while its copies get faster

The probe ends its warm-up once NVML reads every link at its full PCIe generation, then timed five copies to each
tier. A link can read so before it copies at that rate: in one captured start the probe ended after 0.09 s and the
RTX 5070 Ti's five copies read 7.3 GB/s (54 in every other start), below the 20 GB/s that turns a tier's prefetch on,
and with --second-gpu auto that reading would also have ranked it behind an RTX 3090 on an x4 link. 14 of ~3,750
recorded fixed-text runs here started without that card's prefetch, 8 of them in one day: with two GPUs IQ3_S's code
text then ran 19% slower (189 t/s against 211), with three within noise.

It now times five more for as long as a five's best is 5% above the best before (40 fives at most): a link that is at
its rate stops after the second five. 150 starts of IQ3_S's config: the 5070 Ti at 53.0-55.6 GB/s in every one, the
probe 0.39-0.80 s (median 0.62; 0.36-0.71 before).

--second-gpu-clocks: a tier's clocks locked through NVML while the engine generates

A tier that gets nothing but the verify windows' short shares and drives no display is slowed by the Windows driver
between them: this PC's second RTX 3090, the third tier, falls to P5-P8, its rows come late and its moves between
windows copy at 1.6 GB/s instead of 6.3. Locked with nvidia-smi it is fast, and draws ~110 W instead of ~12 whenever
a model is loaded.

--second-gpu-clocks C[,..] (off by default; a value per tier, <graphics min>-<graphics max>/<memory> in MHz, 0 for a
tier left alone) sets NVML's locked clocks from a thread of core::GpuClocks: at a request's start when its batched
prompt part is at most a chunk, else as that part's last chunk begins, and releases them 5 s after the request, when
the engine ends, at std::exit and before the _Exit of a CUDA fault. NVML refuses a process without administrator
rights: the engine says so once and goes on at the driver's clocks. A lock an engine was killed with stays until the
next engine's first release or nvidia-smi -rgc -rmc.

#M10 Paged engines: size the GPU pool to dedicated memory; copy-back rule

On Windows with a BIOS share (Strix Halo), a GPU pool sized past what
Windows really gives the process spilled into shared memory and slowed
prompts (ds41 at --gpu-mib 61440: -24%). No reported figure gives the
real limit: it depends on allocation sizes and is shared by every
program. gpu_local_memory now reads the share through D3DKMT segment
statistics, and get_share_top (paged_start.cpp) takes 256 MiB pool
chunks at the first sizing until one lands in shared memory, then gives
them back; the room is that level minus what all programs hold now.
A --gpu-mib above the room is cut, with a log line. Linux and discrete
GPUs keep the old rule. Measured: ds41 at 61440 gets a 50.2-53.7 GiB
pool and the before-lending prompt speeds.

The copy-back rule replaces the "2x" rule: an expert evicted from the
GPU is copied to RAM when GPU->RAM copying beats the SSD by 1.0x for a
lend's evictions and 1.2x for the others (is_copy_back_worth), and only
into free RAM pages or over the least-used RAM expert of that size whose
decayed count is lower (RamExperts::keep_copy). Copies finish inside the
lend, before the pages become prompt buffers, and the RAM pool now lends
before the GPU so fresh copies don't land in its lent run. Old and new
rules measured the same within thermal drift.

### Also

- docs: replace the "2x" wording in DETAILS.md and the plan; record the
  results under M10.

engine: --conversation-cache-park-ssd: parked conversations live in the SSD folder only, written as deltas

With --conversation-cache-park-ssd (needs --conversation-cache-spill-dir; off by default) no parked conversation
stays in RAM and no K/V copy of the live conversation is kept for the next park, so more agents can take turns on
one stream without more memory.

- A conversation's K/V has its own store file (conversation_kv_store: every part at a fixed place, sparse). A park
  writes only the bytes that changed since the file was read back; its running state goes to a meta file and each
  checkpoint to its own write-once file (--conversation-cache-park-ssd-deepest-checkpoint keeps one,
  -checkpoints N the shallowest and the N deepest, -whole the old whole-file park, -keep-pct when a file is updated
  in place).
- --conversation-cache-park-ssd-stream: a read-back streams the K/V from its file into the session, no copy in RAM.
  A file that cannot be streamed is dropped and the request reads its prompt.
- --conversation-cache-park-on-exit: the conversation in use is parked at a clean stop and read back at the next start.
- The folder's drive is measured once at the first start (--conversation-cache-spill-probe-mib / -probe-s, 0 = off);
  the restore-or-read gate uses the measured read speed unless --conversation-cache-spill-mbps sets one.
- index.log is written again from the live entries above --conversation-cache-spill-index-mib (64; 0 = never); the
  new log replaces the old one only when all of it is on the disk.
- The automatic RAM cache's share and cap are options (--conversation-cache-auto-pct, -auto-max-mib), also for the
  PLE lock check.
- STRATA_SPILL_STORE_VERIFY=1 (a test switch) compares a written file with its source bytes and a restored session
  with its file.
- A filesystem without sparse files is refused for the K/V store (the park is skipped with a log line).

#M10 Paged engines: lend prompt buffers from the page pools per prompt

strata-q38 held its prompt buffers for the whole run beside its page
pool (1.0 GiB of GPU memory and 0.36 GiB of page-locked RAM at 2,048-
token chunks on the Strix Halo); on 8 GB cards that is an eighth of the
card. The owner wants no permanent prompt buffers: each prompt borrows
them from the pools and gives them back.

- GPU virtual memory: each GPU pool is one reserved virtual range whose
  chunks are mapped back to back; a shrink unmaps from the top. The
  shared vmm code now runs on HIP as well as CUDA. Measured on the
  Strix Halo (HIP 7.1): a mapped range reads, writes and random-reads
  at the speed of hipMalloc (231 vs 227 GB/s read); mapping costs
  ~5 ms a 256 MiB chunk, paid only on resize. Without virtual memory a
  lend stays inside the top chunk.
- page_pool: experts pack upward from the conversations' reserve, so
  spare pages collect at the top; lend takes a run from the top: free
  pages first, then moves experts into free pages (keeping the
  prompt's own K/V room, which make_room reserves first), then evicts;
  conversation blocks in the way move and their tables are rewritten.
  Chunks of one virtual range are joined, so runs may cross them.
- paged_engine: each prompt reads in the largest chunk up to the
  ceiling (--prefill N; auto or none: 8,192) that the pools can lend
  then, in steps of 256 tokens, and fails with a reason below 256; the
  buffers go back when the read ends and the evicted experts refill.
  A model supplies only the bytes a chunk needs and the layout at an
  address (Prefill::relayout for Qwen3.8; DeepSeek still allocates its
  own, see M10).
- Memory panel: lent pages show as "Prompt buffers" in their own colour.

serve: restore a session file without holding its K/V in RAM

The RESTORE path materialized the whole snapshot in host memory, so a deep
session could not be restored on a machine that serves it: upstream's own
documented 503 'when the RAM to read the file is not there'.  The restore is
now two passes over the same file, format v1 unchanged:

- the read pass parses and validates the whole file (running state, K/V
  headers, every count against this session's limits, the payload hash)
  without materializing the K/V; it reports each layer's part sizes.
- the apply pass re-reads the file and copies the K/V into the authoritative
  pools a 16 MiB block at a time.  It is bound to the read pass: a file whose
  layer count or any part size differs is refused before that part is applied,
  and the payload hash is compared to the trailer at the end.  The first
  applied block is the gate - before it a failure refuses cleanly, after it
  the engine fail-stops rather than decode from bytes it cannot vouch for.

Peak RAM is two 16 MiB buffers and the running-state metadata, so a session
of any depth restores under the same floor.  Measured on a 198,830-token
IQ3_S session: 3.05 GiB restored in 3.4-3.5 s, next turn 99.99% reused.
The residency refill after the pool writes is mandatory for the modes that
keep K/V in VRAM and runs per layer (kv_stream_reset / kv_ring_restore).

line says "(parked in MWAITX)".

energy counter over the generating seconds: on three GPUs 61-76 W with the spin, 56-71 W with the wait (IQ3_S 63 ->

prompt cache: the parked conversations take no RAM below --ram-reserve-mib available, and give it back between requests when the system runs below it

  memory; 0: the budget alone, as before).

  bytes now plus that, the least recently used leaving to make room as for the budget; nothing is evicted for a
  conversation the spare RAM would not hold with the park empty.
- ConversationCache::shed / PromptCache::shed, after each request: below the reserve, the least recently used parked
  conversations leave until their bytes cover the deficit, and the idle checkpoint buffers are freed, pinned ones
  too (the free list keeps up to 17 pinned ones, so the evicted chains did not give their RAM back).

serve: a marker the reply quotes stays text, and a turn that ends mid-structure is continued

A control token's text cannot be generated: the literal re-tokenizes to the token that stops the
turn, so a reply quoting `<|im_end|>` was cut at the quote and ended as "stop" with nothing after it
(#537's shape, for the turn-end token).  The stop branch now reads the shape the token arrives in -
one backtick left over on its line, a ``` block open in the answer or in the thinking, or the
thinking with no code open - and in each of those the marker's text is written back as ordinary text
(#931's `plain` mechanism) and the turn goes on from there, bounded by QUOTED_MARKER_MAX and, for a
reply that only repeats the marker with no newline in between, by QUOTED_MARKER_RUN_MAX.  A turn-end
inside an unclosed block or inside the thinking is not an end either: the answer is continued instead
of stopping mid-structure.  Shape 3's exception is #728's loop - thinking that repeats whole passages
is a loop running on until the model writes its own end, not a marker the thought mentions, so
reasoning_repeat_coverage decides and the turn ends where the model ended it (which is what
serve/test_reasoning_loop_recovery.py expects: one pass with the recovery off).

OutputParser tracks the backtick run of the text that goes out - the content and the reasoning
region, tool arguments out, a run counted when it ends so one split across deltas counts once, a span
not reaching across its line - so the serve can tell a quoted marker from an ordinary turn-end:
`tick_run` (the run under the cursor), `quoted_marker` (that backtick is the one left over on its
line) and `unclosed_code`.  That is a second read of the same text next to #1058's `_track`
(`fence`/`line`/`ticks`), which answers where the NEXT character would sit - a paragraph's backtick
count, a fence opened at a line start - and cannot say what the character under the cursor is.  A
stop token with calls waiting in `pending` is #1058's settling point for a call written inside the
thinking, so it ends the turn rather than being read as a quote.  The stop ids get one source, the
tokenizer's control tokens, so the engine's --eos-ids, the serve's stopping and the write-back agree
(stop_texts, END_OF_TEXT); the thinking's text is kept as a capped tail (LOOP_TEXT_MAX) because both
the #728 look and the stop branch read it.

serve: STRATA_PARK_TRUNCATE, park the prefix that fits

Parking refuses whole: when the outgoing chain does not fit the cache
byte budget or the physical-RAM floor, the entire snapshot is dropped
and the next request of that conversation re-reads from the root (or
token 0) - measured 225 s for a 160k-token chain.  The chain itself is
a depth ruler: walk it deepest-first and park the first checkpoint
prefix that passes both gates instead.  The parked copy keeps root +
chain + K/V [0, L), and mounts live on that checkpoint's running state
(the session state is deeper than L).  The next request mounts the
prefix and re-reads only the tail - the reply plus the new turn, which
the client re-renders anyway.  Single-stage only (the layer-split path
has no per-checkpoint byte split to walk); the below-min-tokens gate
already passed for the full chain and a truncated copy is parked even
under it - a root-deep mirror still saves the shared prefix.  The same
rule works the other way: an already-parked entry asked to make room
is shrunk to one of its own checkpoints (K/V pages past the landing,
the deeper checkpoints' running states and their ids go, the landing's
state moves into live) before it is dropped whole; a landing below
--conversation-cache-min-tokens is not worth a slot and the entry goes
whole.  Truncation obeys the borrowed-donor guard the same way eviction does:
shrinking a donor mid-restore would put the borrowed prefix outside
the donor (the restore ERR).  Off unless STRATA_PARK_TRUNCATE=1; the
environment variable is the only switch (no flag).

cache: hand the parked copy's spread checkpoints back to a slot-mounted chain

A batch slot keeps at most one checkpoint of the conversation it serves, so
every main-chain switch that returns through a slot (slot_source mount)
rebuilds the checkpoint pool from that single point. The checkpoints the read
spread along the chain survive only on the parked copy, and the truncate-park
ladder (STRATA_PARK_TRUNCATE) starves of shallow rungs: measured overnight, a
205k chain parked under RAM pressure skipped whole ("skip parking (physical
RAM admission; need 5949 MiB ...)") because its only remaining checkpoints sat
at >=196k and every shallower rung had been lost to a switch.

(cvec match, prefix-compatible checkpoints) and copies back every
prefix-compatible point the chain does not already hold. The used stamps
travel, so returned survivors age from their last hit and the normal
retention policy thins them again. Text only for now: an empty image list
never matches a checkpoint that carries image keys. STRATA_POOL_RESTORE=0
turns the return off (default on).

Where qsa_prompt_attn_batch refuses (RDNA2 gfx103x, no WMMA), the prompt reads
every QSA layer's attention through the decode kernels, 32 queries a call:

v_dot2_f32_f16, FP32 accumulation - the tensor-core prompt kernels' input
precision). k8v4 pools only; anything else falls through to the usual path.
